title: Reconfigurable Retina-Inspired Looming Detection
problem: Detecting rapidly approaching objects and potential threats requires efficient real-time detection. Current systems lack specialized hardware optimized for retinal looming detection computation.
motivation: Retina-inspired systems can enable real-time collision detection and threat avoidance with energy-efficient in-sensor computation.
method: A novel reconfigurable CMOS circuit is designed for looming detection based on retinal neuroscience principles. Performance is validated using real-world laboratory data and hardware-aware simulations. The circuit is implemented in GlobalFoundries' 22nm FD-SOI technology with measured energy efficiency of 0.36 pJ per looming spike for a 5×5 pixel kernel.
key_novelty: A reconfigurable CMOS circuit specifically designed for retinal looming detection with in-sensor computation capabilities.
contributions: Reconfigurable CMOS circuit architecture for looming detection based on retinal neuroscience
Validation on real-world laboratory data demonstrating collision detection accuracy
Implementation and characterization in 22nm FD-SOI technology with 0.36 pJ/spike energy consumption
Hardware-software co-design framework integrating neuromorphic principles with modern CMOS

metrics.accuracy: High collision detection accuracy with low false-positives (quantitative values not provided)
